I fixed `slugify()` in `textkit/slug.py`. The regex now matches runs of non-alphanumerics (`[^a-z0-9]+`) and the result is stripped of leading and trailing dashes, so `'Hello,  World!'` should now give `'hello-world'`.

`bb-test` passes (2 tests). I didn't add a test for the reported case, and I couldn't run a direct check of the example because a shell command was denied.

--- a/textkit/slug.py
+++ b/textkit/slug.py
@@ -4,4 +4,4 @@
 def slugify(text):
     """Lowercase ASCII slug: runs of non-alphanumerics become one dash."""

-    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")
